title: the case for lowercase
gist: Wired traces all-lowercase writing from 1960s single-case teletypes and Unix hacker culture through 4chan and Tumblr feminism to its present use as a status, intimacy and possibly anti-AI signal. The piece argues its meaning keeps being reassigned, with the author's own subject switching back to capitals.

insights.claim: Early 1950s computer terminals supported only 64 characters, leaving no room for lowercase, so early languages like Fortran, Pascal and Lisp were written in uppercase; lowercase arrived as hardware matured and memory costs fell in the 1960s-70s.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Character-set limits set by hardware cost shaped long-lived software and writing conventions.

insights.claim: Unix, begun in 1969 by Ken Thompson and colleagues at Bell Labs on a PDP-7, supported two cases, which forced the research and corporate world to standardize capitalization in code (snake_case versus SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE) that hardened into etiquette.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Tooling choices at one lab propagated into global norms of legibility and tone.

insights.claim: Ken Thompson, 83, told the author via an all-lowercase email that lowercase 'started with single-case tty model 33. now, it is habit.'
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: A primary-source claim that lowercase is a legacy habit, not an aesthetic.
insights.quote: lower case? it started with single-case tty model 33. now, it is habit

insights.claim: The September 1993 move by AOL to offer Usenet access brought a flood of newcomers using proper capitalization, making the lowercase hacker vernacular a marginal quirk and proper capitalization the norm.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Mass onboarding of non-technical users reset internet norms; a template for later platform-entry shifts.
insights.locator: point is, the internet used to be nerd country

insights.claim: The author concludes lowercase was not invented by Tumblr users and 'has always been the hallmark of the outsider'.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Style tends to originate in out-groups and be adopted later by the mainstream.

insights.claim: For one side of the internet lowercase reads as feminine: writer Rayne Fisher-Quann says it neutralizes the self-importance of personal writing and is a way 'to avoid criticism', a style she traces to early-2010s feminist Tumblr.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Self-deprecating stylistic signalling is a defensive strategy in public online writing.
insights.locator: for one side of the internet

insights.claim: Rupi Kaur's lowercase 'Milk and Honey' outsold the next-best-selling poetry work (The Odyssey) by a factor of 10 in 2016, cementing lowercase as an expression of accessible vulnerability.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Lowercase aesthetics demonstrably moved mass-market sales, not just niche culture.

insights.claim: Linguist Adam Aleksic argues the lowercase habit is not specifically feminine since 4chan and other mega online communities also skip regular punctuation and use text-markup like asterisks for emphasis.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Informal-text norms appear across online subcultures with different politics.

insights.claim: Gretchen McCulloch's 'resemanticization' theory says a form coined for one function (lol as laugh out loud) acquires a secondary meaning as usage spreads, so lowercase now carries no link to hacker or feminist origins.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Marker meanings drift quickly, so reading intent from style is unreliable.
insights.locator: of course, maybe none of this matters

insights.claim: Gong.io reportedly analyzed over 85 million cold emails and found lowercase subject lines get twice as many opens as properly capitalized ones.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Lowercase has measurable commercial value in outbound marketing, though a novelty effect could fade as it spreads.
insights.quote: those with lowercase subject lines get twice as many opens as properly capitalized ones do

insights.claim: Lowercase also works as a status marker: Jack Dorsey announced a 40 percent staff layoff in February in an all-lowercase tweet, and a tech growth investor says the more senior you get, the less formal your emails are.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Informality in tone from senior leaders signals power, including for sensitive announcements.
insights.locator: lowercase can also be a status symbol

insights.claim: Aleksic offers that people may now write in lowercase to signal they are not AI, because AI can write lowercase but must be prompted to, adding friction.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Human-authenticity signalling via stylistic imperfection is an emerging response to AI text, though easily mimicked.

insights.claim: Some people say lowercase reads as less intense: the author has heard of peers who 'become lowercase' because capitals in texts and dating apps seem too intense.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: Typographic tone norms shape digital intimacy.
insights.locator: i've heard of people my age

insights.claim: The piece ends on irony: after Aleksic calls lowercase the new normal, Fisher-Quann's Substack now uses proper capitalization.
insights.speaker: Tiffany Ng
insights.so_what: The trend is already being reversed by an early adopter, a possible sign of saturation.
